basis: Autoinflammatory arthritis; pleuritis occurs in 30-79%. Hepatitis is 5-29%; enzyme elevations alone do not establish sustained liver damage. Evanescent rash excluded.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatitis occurs in 5-29%; frequent hepatomegaly and enzyme elevations alone do not establish substantial lasting hepatic damage.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia; vitreoretinopathy 80-99%, hearing impairment 30-79%. Characteristic cleft palate is reported in 1/1, though that frequency has a small denominator.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: cleft palate is a characteristic structural oral defect, reported in 1/1 annotated patients; frequency evidence is limited by the small sample.

basis: Arterial cholesterol embolization directly causes renal ischemic injury in roughly 50-80% and cutaneous ischemic lesions in roughly 35% or more.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous ischemic lesions occur in approximately 35% or more; embolic tissue ischemia represents direct injury rather than a transient inflammatory rash.

basis: Bone fragility and skeletal dysplasia define disease. Acanthosis nigricans in 3/5 and blue sclerae in 4/5 do not establish functional damage; insulin resistance is only 1/5.

decisions.dermatologic: none: acanthosis nigricans occurs in 3/5, but thickening and pigmentation alone do not establish substantial skin damage or loss of function.

basis: Marrow disease and diagnostic skin/nail changes and oral leukoplakia; pulmonary fibrosis 3/6. Hepatic fibrosis 2/6 and osteoporosis 3/6 omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic fibrosis in 2/6 qualifies by frequency, but is omitted under the cap while retaining defining marrow/mucocutaneous disease and pulmonary fibrosis in 3/6.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral leukoplakia is part of the major diagnostic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita; the oral mucosa belongs to this axis.

basis: High-grade osteoid-producing bone malignancy; pulmonary metastases directly occupy lung in approximately 30-40% over the typical disease course.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung metastases affect approximately 30-40% over the disease course; they are direct spread of this malignancy, rather than a separate disease whose risk is increased.

basis: Defining digital and skeletal malformations; dental open bite is persistent malocclusion reported in 30-79%. Hearing impairment and intellectual disability occur in 5-29%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental open bite in 30-79% represents persistent defective occlusion; high palate and facial appearance alone would not justify this axis.

basis: Digital skeletal defects and cleft palate/glossoptosis define disease; ventricular septal defects occur in 30-79%. Chronic otitis media is a separately diagnosed secondary disease.

decisions.otologic: none: chronic otitis media occurs in 30-79%, but is a separate secondary disease associated with palatal dysfunction, rather than intrinsic ear damage from the syndrome.

basis: Hormone resistance and AHO skeletal defects; intellectual disability and cataracts each 30-79%. Subcutaneous ossification (2/2) and enamel defects (30-79%) omitted under cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts are damaging lens disease reported in 30-79%; retained under the cap because of their visual consequences.
decisions.dermatologic: none: characteristic subcutaneous ossification qualifies, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of common cognitive and visual impairment.

basis: Primary B-cell deficiency impairs antibody production. Recurrent infections are separately diagnosed diseases; rash and diarrhea do not establish intrinsic organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a B-cell deficiency with impaired lymphocyte development; B lymphocytes are blood cells, so the explicit blood-cell disease rule applies.
